answer:
To draw the sectional front view and true shape of the hexagonal prism:

1. **Initial Position**: Draw the top view as a regular hexagon of $25\text{ mm}$ side with two parallel sides perpendicular to the VP (since a face rests on the HP and axis is parallel to VP, the top view shows the hexagonal base). Project the front view, which will be a rectangle of $65\text{ mm}$ height and width equal to the distance across corners/flats depending on orientation.
2. **Section Plane**: The cutting plane is perpendicular to HP and inclined at $45^\circ$ to VP. In the top view, draw the cutting plane making $45^\circ$ with the reference line (VP) passing through a point $20\text{ mm}$ from one end along the axis.
3. **Sectional Front View**: Project the intersection points from the top view onto the corresponding generators in the front view. Join these points with straight lines and hatch the section region at $45^\circ$.
4. **True Shape**: Draw an auxiliary reference line parallel to the cutting line in the top view. Project perpendiculars from the cutting points on the top view to this auxiliary line. Transfer the distances of these points from the X-Y line (from the front view) onto the respective projectors to obtain the true shape.
proTip: Always project the true shape perpendicular to the auxiliary cutting plane line to preserve actual dimensions.
